$comment: Provenance is written by hand. Sizes and SHA-256 sums are generated into manifest.json by scripts/build_manifest.py and must never be edited here. `collection` says which body of work a file belongs to; `stage` says whether the file is a third-party input (`original`) or something this project derived from one (`converted`). `modified_from_supplied` is set when an `original` artifact is not byte-identical to what the supplier sent, and says exactly what was changed; the SHA-256 then records our copy and cannot be checked against the supplier's. The two are separate axes, so a request for the converted GIAMIP data can be expressed. `permission` records whether the supplier has agreed to redistribution through https://data.gadopt.org/gia-mip/: one of `granted`, `requested`, `not_asked`. An artifact whose permission is not `granted` is never uploaded and is never fetched.

spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz.description: The COST Action ES0701 benchmark submission tree: contributor data, GMT plotting scripts, Fortran filters and PostScript figures for tests 1/1 to 7/1 and 1/2 to 3/2.
spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz.source_citation: Spada, G., Barletta, V. R., Klemann, V., Riva, R. E. M., Martinec, Z., Gasperini, P., Lund, B., Wolf, D., Vermeersen, L. L. A. and King, M. A. (2011). A benchmark study for glacial isostatic adjustment codes. Geophysical Journal International 185(1), 106-132.
spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz.notes: A working copy, not a curated release. Forty-seven operating-system and GMT state files were removed before packing: .DS_Store, .gmtcommands4, .gmtdefaults4 and .GMT_bb_info. Nothing else was changed. The eleven README files inside T02* document the VILMA column layout and are part of the record.
spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz.modified_from_supplied: Packed into a tar archive from a directory tree, with forty-seven files removed: eighteen .DS_Store, fourteen .gmtcommands4, fourteen .gmtdefaults4 and one .GMT_bb_info. No file that was kept was changed. The 977 members and their individual sums are listed in the manifest and can be checked against the supplier's tree file by file.

martinec2018/benchmarkA.zip.description: Benchmark A: contributor profiles, difference files against the VEGA reference, and the GMT script that drew figure 3.
martinec2018/benchmarkA.zip.source_citation: Martinec, Z., Klemann, V., van der Wal, W., Riva, R. E. M., Spada, G., Sun, Y., Melini, D., Kachuck, S. B., Barletta, V., Simon, K., A, G. and James, T. martinec2018/benchmarkA.zip.notes: Assembled 2022-10-20. Z_ZM_load.out holds one row, so the VEGA reference profile for benchmark A is absent and must be reconstructed. The benchmark page cited in the paper, geofjv.troja.mff.cuni.cz/GIABenchmark/, no longer answers.

martinec2018/benchmarkB.zip.description: Benchmark B: contributor profiles through the ice centre and the basin centre, difference files, the GMT scripts for figures 5 and 6, and uprav.out, the VEGA sea-level grid used for figure 4.
martinec2018/benchmarkB.zip.notes: Internal case code C2 is published case B. Both VEGA reference files are present, on two different colatitude grids.

martinec2018/sbk_benchmark_data.tar.gz.description: Samuel Kachuck's giapy submission: internal case codes A, C2, D3, E2 and F1, each with four cross-sections.
martinec2018/sbk_benchmark_data.tar.gz.source_citation: See martinec2018/benchmarkA.zip. The code is Kachuck, S. B. (2017), giapy, https://github.com/skachuck/giapy.
martinec2018/sbk_benchmark_data.tar.gz.supplier: unknown; obtained through the G-ADOPT reference collection
martinec2018/sbk_benchmark_data.tar.gz.notes: Only two of the five internal case codes are tied to a published case letter. A is case A. C2 is case B, because two of its files are byte-identical to files in benchmarkB.zip. D3, E2 and F1 are unresolved. The A profile in this archive supersedes the one in benchmarkA.zip; see corrections.json.

martinec2018/giapy_sle_test.py.description: Kachuck's driver script for the sea-level benchmark, dated 2017-09-19.

martinec2018/giapy_sle_test.py.notes: Its load and time labels are shifted by one from the published tables, and its basin list holds a basin the paper does not use. It generates A, D1, D2, E1, E2 and F1, and contains no code for C2 or D3, so it cannot settle the case mapping on its own.

giamip/ice-history.zip.description: Six global ice-thickness histories interpolated onto the prescribed Gauss-Legendre grid: ICE-6G_D, ICE-7G_NA, PaleoMIST 1a and GLAC3c profiles 1, 2 and 3.
giamip/ice-history.zip.source_citation: GIAMIP input distribution. The underlying reconstructions are third-party and each carries its own terms: ICE-6G_D (Peltier, Argus and Drummond), ICE-7G_NA (Roy and Peltier), PaleoMIST (Gowan et al. 2021), GLAC3 (Tarasov, unpublished).
giamip/ice-history.zip.supplier: GIAMIP organisers, through the shared input folder
giamip/ice-history.zip.notes: The protocol table names GLAC3b; the filenames say GLAC3c_profile; the internal title and source attributes say GLAC3c_merge. All six files declare _FillValue = 0.0 on ice_thickness. PaleoMIST starts at 80 ka with 379 steps; the other five start at 122 ka with 463.

giamip/initial-topography.zip.description: Three present-day bed elevations on the prescribed grid, differing only in the Antarctic source: BedMachine Antarctica v3, Bedmap3 or Bedmap2, each merged with BedMachine Greenland v5.5 and GEBCO.
giamip/initial-topography.zip.source_citation: GIAMIP input distribution. Fretwell et al. (2013) Bedmap2; Pritchard et al. (2025) Bedmap3; Morlighem et al. (2020) BedMachine; GEBCO.
giamip/initial-topography.zip.supplier: GIAMIP organisers, through the shared input folder
giamip/initial-topography.zip.notes: The source attribute of the BedMachine Antarctica v3 file names BedMachine Greenland twice and never names its Antarctic dataset. The other two files are correct. All three reference a grid_mapping variable named crs that does not exist in the file.

giamip/giamip-protocol-v2.4.md.notes: Converted from .docx. The two embedded equation images are kept as base64 data URIs. The prose is unchanged.

martinec2018/benchmarkA-Z_ZM_load-full.o.description: A full VEGA reference profile for benchmark A: 1441 rows of colatitude 0 to 180 at 0.125 degree spacing, seven columns, with a column header. Supplied to replace the single-row Z_ZM_load.out in benchmarkA.zip.
martinec2018/benchmarkA-Z_ZM_load-full.o.notes: This is benchmark A: vertical displacement is -302.6 m at colatitude 0, and benchmark A is the only case whose cap sits at the pole. It is NOT the run behind published figure 3. Recomputing any contributor's difference against it misses the shipped difference file by an RMS of 0.057 m, and all four contributors tested miss by nearly the same amount, which places the discrepancy in this file and not in them. The disagreement is a smooth bump centred on the cap edge at colatitude 10, reaching 0.56 m there and falling to 0.003 m beyond 90 degrees. Degrees 0 and 1 explain 1.5 per cent of it, so it is not the degree-2 start the paper records for benchmark A. Section 5.1 of the paper says the cap edge converges extremely slowly with cut-off degree, which is the most likely cause. Kept alongside the reconstructed reference, not in place of it. Its header is the only documentation of the seven-column VEGA format used by twenty benchmark B files.
